world.goal:
📝 Bring node01 (Team Alpha) back to Ready.
Fix must survive a reboot.

scenes.say: Welcome to your software company. Upstairs is the leadership room: the control plane. Jira, the API server, takes every request and checks permissions. Jira's database, etcd, holds the truth. The work assigner, the scheduler, gives each new work item to a team with capacity. And the Release Train Engineer, the controller manager, keeps reality matching the plan.

Downstairs is Team Alpha's room: node zero one. The team lead, the container runtime, gets the developers working. And the Scrum Master, the kubelet, takes the assigned work, and at every sync reports to Jira: team healthy!
scenes.sub: kubelet = Scrum Master → reports "team healthy" at every sync

scenes.say: But today, the Scrum Master doesn't show up. No sync, no report. After forty seconds, the Release Train Engineer marks Team Alpha as not reporting: node zero one, Not Ready. And the work assigner stops giving the team new work.
scenes.sub: No report for 40 s → node01 NotReady → no new work

scenes.say: Your exam task: bring node zero one back to Ready. And the fix must survive a reboot. Remember that last part.
Quick question. Why is node zero one Not Ready?

quiz.t: 🧑‍🔧 The Team Lead (container runtime) is off sick
quiz.fb: Not quite. Without the team lead the work would stall, but the Scrum Master would still report. Nobody is reporting at all.

quiz.t: 🧑‍💼 The Scrum Master (kubelet) isn't doing the job
quiz.fb: Exactly! No Scrum Master, no team healthy report, so the team is marked Not Ready.
Not quite. If Jira were down, nobody could see anything, not even k get nodes.

scenes.say: So go to the team's room. S S H node zero one. Your terminal now works inside Team Alpha's room. Look at the prompt: it says node zero one.
scenes.sub: ssh node01 = walk into Team Alpha's room

scenes.say: Every role in the room has an official assignment. That's system control. System control status kubelet asks: is the Scrum Master doing the job? Answer: inactive, dead. Nobody is.
scenes.sub: systemctl = role assignment · status = is anyone doing the job?

scenes.roster: kubelet · active (running) · covering this sprint only
scenes.say: Easy fix: system control start kubelet. Someone covers the role for this sprint. The Scrum Master reports again, Team Alpha is Ready. Done? Not so fast.
scenes.sub: systemctl start = cover the role… this sprint only

scenes.say: Twist! Next week there's a reorg. That's a reboot. And Team Alpha has no Scrum Master again! Why? Start only covered the role for one sprint. Nobody was officially assigned.
scenes.sub: TWIST: reorg (reboot) → no Scrum Master again

scenes.say: So which command officially assigns the Scrum Master, and starts the job right now?

quiz.fb: That's the trap we just fell into. Start only covers this sprint.
Yes! Enable makes the assignment official, so it survives every reorg. Dash dash now also starts it right away.
That command doesn't exist. And kubectl only talks to Jira, not to the role assignments in the team room.

scenes.say: System control enable, dash dash now, kubelet. Enable: officially assigned, so the role survives every reorg. Dash dash now: start right now.
scenes.sub: enable = official, survives reboots · --now = right now

scenes.say: Another reorg. And this time? The Scrum Master is still there. The fix survives a reboot.
scenes.sub: Reorg again → Scrum Master still there ✓

scenes.say: Go back to the leadership room with exit, and check Jira with k get nodes. Node zero one: Ready. Task done!
scenes.sub: exit = back to leadership · k get nodes = check Jira

scenes.say: Remember: Not Ready means the Scrum Master, the kubelet, isn't doing the job. Go to the team with S S H. Check with status. And never just start it: enable dash dash now, so it survives the reorg.
scenes.sub: NotReady → ssh → status → enable --now → exit → get nodes

steps.do: Go to Team Alpha's room and check the Scrum Master
Assign officially and start now, then go back
